facts: VNC no-clients branch returns before graphic_hw_update; a live client requests regular hardware updates through the adaptive refresh loop.
QMP screendump schedules and waits one graphic_hw_update. ADP declares no async update flag; that callback ends after dirty scan and OUTPUT_READY IRQ, not after guest submission.
Guest write0x4602c bit12 later schedules draw BH, which reads/composites GP buffers, signals dpy update and FRAME_PROCESSED. This is a separate guest-response path.
QMP takes the current surface image reference while BQL held. Its source explicitly allows updates during later save yields, so neither a fixed stale frame nor atomic presentation is guaranteed.
inference: Sparse captures with no VNC may observe an earlier composed surface, then stimulate subsequent guest rendering. Reconnected VNC can restore regular refresh and reveal current Clock elapsed values.
This is consistent with53 observations but exact pipeline lag is unmeasured; do not label it one-frame latency or a guest monotonic-clock defect.
CPU observations during no-VNC interval therefore describe that refresh cadence, not continuous fully presented stopwatch animation.
